ateret-zekenim/1:ב: (ב) that he eats (see words of Orach Chayim s.k. 7) and concludes: since known to all they kindle in winter house where they do not eat, and known each has nearby immediately by eating place a sleeping place — sleeping place is called well for kindling in sleeping place; but one who eats occasionally once or even regularly and sleeping place is far from eating place — then kindle in sleeping place; see further in Shaarei Yeshuvah siman 73. Per the distinction I wrote, both are upheld — Rama's Hagahah and words of Chami Zekeni Maharari cited above.
ateret-zekenim/4:_: Makes a bonfire for him. It appears all leftover oil even more than kindling measure — only oil in the candle designated for kindling requires bonfire as Bach wrote siman 66 — end; so explicitly Ran Bava Metzia and Tosafot chapter Kirah; so Avudraham in name of Rabbenu Shlomo; also another answer: Chazal equated it to holy utensils because reminder of holy oil. What Bach questioned — Beit Yosef wrote in siman 672 if he put more he may extinguish after time passed and may use afterward, etc. — appears difference: certainly may extinguish to kindle other candles and use its light; nevertheless must burn in manner requiring genizah as Avudraham — examine per this Bach's strains unnecessary — this appears plain, finding most poskim agree — Bach's strain void — examine. Some say leftover from day one kindle immediately night two — at end no remedy; also delaying forbidden lest mishap; nevertheless not called shiluach; nullified in sixty; less than sixty no nullification even by kindling. What ruled above after kindling measure may extinguish and do as he wishes — speaks where he put more than measure; where only measure and it went out or wick bad and tangled — forbidden (Rashal siman 85); however what he wrote even if put more requires genizah as I wrote for halacha.
biur-halacha/1:ג: (ג) With him, etc. — see Peri Megadim Orach Chayim letter 3: if two householders in one room and do not rely on each other and each eats his own — requires study if partnership suffices, perhaps each must kindle by law; guest perhaps they were lenient — end; letter 8 brought Levush and Peri Chadash dispute; see Peri Chadash proofs from Maggid Mishneh chapter 4 Hanukkah laws must kindle; from Shibolei Leket Hanukkah siman 185 in name of our rabbis — from his conclusion implies since in one house partnership suffices.
chokhmat-shlomo/1:_: (Seif 1) Guest on whom they do not kindle, etc. NB: See third responsum — since Moharit's words strengthened, etc.; see my essays on Avodah Zarah daf 68a proof for Moharit's view and our explanation inside Sefer HaChaim resolving Maharshal's difficulty on Rashi d.h. le'itot erev — see and examine.
chokhmat-shlomo/3:_: (Same, seif 3) In Hagahah: even if he lodges with gentiles and sees candles, if he wants to be stringent, etc. NB: See Taz who extended; now clear proof for those who forbid stringency from what we learn Berachot 33: difficult — if so say when he makes havdalah on this and not on that, blessings fall on his head; why challenge — say certainly make havdalah on cup not at all in prayer — prayer certainly preferable to cup; only if he makes havdalah in prayer without intent to fulfill, only on cup being d'rabbanan no intent needed; nevertheless if intends not to fulfill — certainly not fulfilled; so truly regarding counting siman 489 — counts with congregation without blessing, intends not to fulfill, blesses later at night — Magen Avraham proves even if intent not required, if intends not to fulfill — not fulfilled though counting then. If so here fits: blessings fall on his head since he truly made havdalah in prayer and on cup — blessing in vain since he intended fulfill havdalah in prayer; nevertheless did not change prayer wording since he also mentioned in prayer — he is among mehaderin; but if he did not make havdalah in prayer at all — worse one who makes havdalah on cup than prayer without cup — why challenge? Must prove like Tosefet Yehuda: if he could have fulfilled through prayer havdalah since he made havdalah again — blessing in vain; not so counting when day and cannot fulfill then. Clear proof in my view. When there I wondered greatly why challenge — perhaps intent: one who makes havdalah on this and that means if first on cup then prayer — blessings fall since then not vain; why challenge? Must be intent: then interruption in prayer — difficult on Rabbeinu Yona Bach Orach Chayim 108 brought mentioning other days' events in prayer is not interruption — learned from if he made havdalah in both he fulfilled; here havdalah must be interruption. Without Rabbeinu Yona — no proof from havdalah — certainly mentioning matter evident not of the day is interruption since evident it is interruption; but havdalah at night — if he did not pray at all he could make havdalah in this prayer — not evident from prayer body it is interruption — not known if he prayed; therefore not evident from body is not interruption. This is Taz's objection; I explained his reason more; even so our question remains: in havdalah on cup first also not evident if already made havdalah on cup — therefore appears main distinction: there prayer draws prayer — if not prayer time no place to pray makeup only because prayer time therefore prays makeup too — obligatory prayer time causes second prayer — one prayer considered; support from generally once permission given, given; not interruption; but if say he made havdalah on cup — no need havdalah in prayer — no havdalah in prayer; if made havdalah — interruption; challenge well. If say like R' Yonah who holds wherever mentioning event matter — not interruption even without this reason — challenge well: why not say intent if first on cup; requires study; proves like Taz not Rabbeinu Yona — examine. Regarding dispute where to begin kindling — see my essays Yoreh De'ah 4th edition siman 280 end daf 162 explanation of Gemara language so mezuzah on right — see and examine well.
chokhmat-shlomo/4:_: (Same, seif 4) Leftover on eighth day of oil for kindling measure, etc. NB: What all found Shulchan Aruch contradictory — see darush Hanukkah year 5560 resolving distinction between prohibition matter and mitzvah matter — see there with God's help. Regarding what all found contradictory to siman 672 — Taz in name of Moharai brought answer: here unspecified oil, there he stipulated only kindling measure; Taz wondered from Gemara chapter Nigmar hadin what he does not see he does not grasp — like Abaye in invitation so Rava in action; we wrote above from this. Now appears per our novellae in Sukkah laws [still in manuscript] to prove not like Hagahot R' Yehoshua Magen Avraham brought — sukkah not forbidden until one sits — invitation not a matter; I proved from what we say: if he set aside seven etrogim for seven days, each fulfills with it and eats next day; if invitation not a matter — in Beit HaShanah not muktzeh — no muktzeh for half Shabbat — why not permitted immediately? Must be invitation is a matter; reason: since sukkah forbidden in benefit from festival "what is festival to God" — in invitation and body of holiness it is a matter as Magen Avraham siman 42; so sukkah; so lulav since we learn lulav from sukkah — see there; so Hanukkah light since similar to menorah as Rashi d.h. hadlakah oseh mitzvah similar to menorah — invitation matter like body of holiness; therefore fits Abaye in invitation alone since only speech not act — what he does not see he does not grasp; so Rava in action with these invitations not a matter — when only act we say why he sees we count act; for permitted part act not counted — end act not done in permitted at all. Here with oil — by invitation alone also forbidden; invitation at act time applies to all — did not know if needed or which part permitted — invitation on all; again if act afterward since invitation and act here all forbidden; act on part helps whole since he invited all — one body; act on part helps whole since invited all; invitation makes one entity; act on stronger part helps whole; all agree; Mechaber's words fit; need not say there stipulated, there without prior invitation only act — Taz's view what he does not see he does not grasp; here he invited all first then kindled — with invitation and act all forbidden; She'iltot source all poskim concluded: since designated for mitzvah why all this — known forbidden from start; intent teaches designated from start with invitation and act together — fits — examine; such my leaning now. Support for distinction: Choshen Mishpat siman 275 seif 7 and Sema — holding gentile property does not acquire until removes bundle and returns; if called on gentile's name acquires all called on his name — see there; so if invitation is matter and all called Hanukkah light — act on part helps all called on its name — see there; if no invitation act on oil does not help rest — examine. Magen Avraham and Peri Chadash forbid keeping for next year lest mishap — difficult: proof there Torah prohibition therefore decree mishap; Hanukkah is itself rabbinic prohibition — why mishap concern — decree on decree? See darush Hanukkah cited — I proved also from this they made like Torah law because of blessing — examine. May leftover oil in Hanukkah lamp be kindled in synagogue to pray by it? Plainly permitted — forbidden in benefit nevertheless mitzvot not given for benefit; even for those holding even rabbinic mitzvot not for benefit — only Torah benefit prohibitions we follow Torah obligation; not obligated in this mitzvah — benefits from Torah like eino metzuveh ve'oseh. Rabbinic benefit prohibition — permitted to fulfill their mitzvah; if follow Torah — permitted entirely; if rabbinic — rabbinically commanded and in matter commanded upon him not for benefit. Hanukkah light from their words — permitted holy use; also in Hanukkah itself some permit holy use; forbidders only while burning for mitzvah — lest holy use not recognizable; or bizuy mitzvah from mitzvah to mitzvah; if remainder burned alone — clear recognition, no bizuy — burning only because forbidden in benefit more bizuy than lighting in synagogue; see Taz similar above siman 154 — even lowering from holiness only if still fit for mitzvah; if not fit — better light mitzvah than genizah; all the more here better holy use than burying — plain to me, need not write; since Peri Megadim in Mishbetzot wrote opposite and permitted only by addition — wrote to remove from that book's heart; in Machatzit HaShekel great error, not as he wrote — examine. (Same seif) Some say may not add to nullify — NB: see my responsum year 5553 Shulchan Aruch Yoreh De'ah siman 69 goose fat law — examine well.
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: (ב) There. Must give perutah, etc. — precise to say perutah: guest need not give half candle cost — perutah given suffices. Some say in Hagahot. Mishna Berurah letter 3: when giving perutah say: I give you this perutah so you acquire for me some oil and wicks in your Hanukkah lights you kindle tonight, or if he wishes all eight nights; homeowner says: I transfer to you some oil with this perutah in my Hanukkah lights I kindle all eight nights. Without perutah homeowner may transfer if he wishes as below letter 5 — say I transfer to you, etc., stand by him at blessing, intend to fulfill through homeowner's blessing; homeowner also intends to discharge him as known.
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: (ג) There. Must give perutah, etc. — appears guest giving expense to homeowner — then must participate; if special room must kindle in room; if guest relies entirely on homeowner — eats from his bread, drinks from his cup — no need, for homeowner who provides all needs will also transfer part of candle money — no suspicion since known he relies on homeowner. Gan HaMelech siman 41. Some say there Shaarei Teshuvah letter 1 Shulchan Gavoah letter 2 in Machatzit — if eats with homeowner on account of all he eats and drinks — needs perutah; if eats as contractor so much per day or week for all needs — no perutah. Appears likewise if homeowner gives all free — no perutah; nevertheless better explicitly say transfer some oil in your Hanukkah lights and homeowner says I transfer, etc., whether paid or free; however what wrote even with special room need not kindle — see below letter 9 — appears same here.
levushei-serad/4:_: {Rama: s.k. 4} As siman 671, etc. In courtyard with two openings — kindle at both, bless only at one not second since only suspicion. One may distinguish: there different since already blessed at one opening — not so here; even though homeowner blessed — in seif 3 Hagahah wrote one may say I do not fulfill through homeowner's blessing — all the more if not partnered with perutah.
magen-avraham/3:_: If he wants. Even though we are not concerned lest he forget since we rely on women even for karet prohibition — nevertheless if he wants to kindle himself he is among mehaderin (Tosefet Yehuda); in responsum Maharil: common custom guests and bachelors kindle since now each kindles — who knows if they kindle for him at home — comes to suspicion; no vain blessing since he does not want to fulfill through wife's — obligation falls on him — end.
magen-avraham/4:א: (א) Required for kindling measure. More than kindling measure — permitted to use l'chatchila as siman 672 seif 2 (Beit Yosef, Mordechai, Rashal, Shulchan Gavoah); Bach ruled if he put oil unspecified — entire oil muktzeh — as Hagahot Maimoniyot and Ran and Tosafot Shabbat daf 44; not so compelled; therefore good to stipulate l'chatchila only measure forbidden; Shulchan Gavoah requires study if he put measure half hour and burned more — may rely on it.
mishnah-berurah/4:ב: (יח) Of oil required, etc. — he gave only kindling measure, went out mid-way and remainder left — forbidden, muktzeh for mitzvah, forbidden to benefit; if he put much in candle and remainder — permitted l'chatchila as above siman 672 seif 2. Know some poskim hold if oil unspecified — entire oil muktzeh unless stipulated l'chatchila only measure forbidden — see above siman 672 Mishna Berurah s.k. 7.
turei-zahav/1:_: Must give perutah to homeowner, etc. Tur HaShulchan siman 101: guest married wanting to kindle with blessing outside house — Gedol A permits — although Gemara: since married I say certainly not obligated; but if he wants may kindle — not vain blessing, among mehaderin. Gedol A: since not obligated called layman if he does — all the more vain blessing since this hidur not in Talmud; TaZ concludes correctly called mehaderin: as hidur of light per person in one house, so hidur man and wife in two places; tanna did not teach this uncommon hidur; since we find mehaderin and mehaderin min hamehaderin — not adding to Talmud detracts — end. Beit Yosef: should not rely to bless unnecessary blessing — end. Rashal in brief rulings: man and wife certainly suffice one light; married guest not knowing wife kindles for him may kindle and bless; if knows clearly she kindles for him — should not kindle unless alone for viewer — kindle without blessing; where he did not know she kindled and came that night — must return kindle and bless — rabbinic obligation fell; where he does not want fulfill through wife's kindling at home — not so important, cannot bless — end. We have not yet seen Rashal's long words; our view TaZ correct: Gedol A's hidur not in Talmud — Gemara mehaderin means each will likely do so, each wants mehaderin; unlike this also in other blessings permission to do as he wishes — if wants fulfill through wife's blessing, if not — bless himself; compare Rosh chapter 3 two who ate must divide — Rashi between zimmun and hamotzi blessings; Rosh: world did not practice; Rashi — not heard practiced hamotzi blessing; incident of bar Kappara, etc. — no prohibition if each blesses hamotzi — Rosh: not practiced; Heaven forbid Rosh say vain blessing — Rashi included even in mitzvah obligation; found in yotzer or blessing — Rosh responsum: I say with shaliach tzibbur calmly though if hears shaliach tzibbur fulfilled — lest not intend well for blesser's words; Beit HaMikdash Beit Yosef 183 in name of Orchot Chayim in name of Rif: each may bless Birkat HaMazon though they invite — cannot intend well, etc.; but like Rambam he would not bless quietly, etc. — we see one may fulfill through friend's blessing and if unwilling — no prohibition, intent for Heaven; one unwilling to bless himself like Rambam — also intent for Heaven not multiply blessings since can fulfill through friend — here too; all the more not with wife, not hearing her blessing — can say I do not fulfill through wife's blessing not in her presence — listener and responder require presence; even at home unwilling through wife's — I know no prohibition if he blesses himself — like minor chinuch age kindling with blessing — plainly fulfills through father's blessing; we see custom all going outside on Hanukkah take Hanukkah lights to kindle where he goes though household kindles with wife — even if household not intending discharge him only themselves — itself difficult why take lights — household with wife can intend discharge him too; rather preferable bless himself as here — Rama ruled so nearby.
turei-zahav/3:_: Makes bonfire for him. What is difficult from here on what written siman 672 permitted to use after kindled measure — I wrote there.
turei-zahav/4:_: That one may not add, etc. Yoreh De'ah siman 99 seif 6 I wrote Shulchan Aruch's words contradict in this ruling and halacha follows Shulchan Aruch there.
levushei-serad/2:_: Section 503 — the laws of Mahariv brought in Darkei Moshe 2; nowadays one does not participate with a perutah even if he has no open door for himself. Magen Avraham explains that he eats in a room alone; therefore in Talmudic times when they kindled at the entrance from outside, since there was only one entrance, participation suffices — not so nowadays when they kindle inside, and since there are two rooms he must kindle alone; but when there is no room alone, even nowadays participation suffices. However on the face of the matter it does not appear so; there is to resolve — requires study.
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (ב) That they do not kindle for him in his house — for by law when his wife kindles the Hanukkah light in his house he fulfills his obligation through her kindling even if he is in a place far from his house, and he need not participate even with a perutah; see Taz in the name of Rashal that specifically when he knows clearly that his wife kindles for him, but if he does not know he must kindle and also bless. For this reason one who did not know they kindled for him and came that night to his house and found they kindled for him must kindle — since he did not know initially, presumably his intent was to kindle himself and not to fulfill through his wife, and automatically the Sages' regulation applies to him; see Magen Avraham that his view is he kindles without a blessing.
